thread.title: Illinois lawmakers approve extension of SALT workaround for small businesses
thread.title_full: Illinois lawmakers approve extension of SALT workaround for small businesses

author: Prairie State Wire
title: Illinois lawmakers approve extension of SALT workaround for small businesses
text:
Brad Close President | National Federation of Independent Business
Brad Close President | National Federation of Independent Business
The Illinois General Assembly has approved legislation that extends the state's SALT (State and Local Taxes) workaround, allowing pass-through businesses such as S-corporations and partnerships to continue deducting state taxes from their federal tax returns.
"Small businesses were relieved when the General Assembly voted to extend the SALT workaround," said NFIB Illinois State Director Noah Finley. "Pass-through businesses—such as S-Corps and partnerships—could have been hit with a higher tax burden next year if Illinois legislators hadn’t voted to make the workaround permanent."
The provision, officially called the Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET), was originally set to expire at the end of 2025. Without legislative action, many Illinois businesses using this tax structure would have faced increased federal tax liabilities starting in 2026.
According to estimates from the Taxpayers’ Federation of Illinois, the SALT workaround provides approximately $500 million in annual savings for businesses in the state.
Representative Curtis Tarver of District 25 led efforts to advance this legislation in the Illinois House. The measure now awaits the governor’s signature before becoming law.
